name: @myspec/mcp-server

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List or search MySpec projects accessible to the authenticated user.

query.description: Search term to filter projects by name. Omit to list all projects.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get details for a project including all active spec sessions, files (id + metadata), and attachments (id + metadata).

project_id.description: UUID of the project to fetch

tools.name: get_spec_file
tools.description: Get spec file metadata. With `include_download_url=N`, also returns a signed, time-limited download URL for revision N (latest or historical). The URL is self-authenticating, so no credentials are returned.

include_download_url.description: Revision number to include a download URL for. Returns a signed, time-limited URL for that revision (latest or historical) that needs no credentials. Omit or 0 to skip.

tools.name: read_spec_file
tools.description: Return a window of a spec file's UTF-8 content, paginated by line (offset/limit, default and cap 2000 lines, 1 MiB per response). Large files are read across multiple calls using `next_offset`. Bytes are cached on disk under the configured cache root (default ~/.myspec) at `project/<projectId>/file/<fileId>/rev/<rev>/<basename>` and reused on subsequent reads of the same revision, so paging through a file downloads it once. Files above 8 MiB and binary content are refused — use download_spec_file to save those to a local file instead.

revision.description: Specific revision number to read (defaults to the latest revision).

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from (default 1; 0 is an alias for 1).

limit.description: Max lines to return (default 2000, capped at 2000; larger values are clamped).

tools.name: download_spec_file
tools.description: Download a spec file's raw bytes to a local file. By default it lands under `.specs/` in the MCP server's working directory, mirroring the file's remote path — pass `destination_path` only to save it somewhere else. Unlike read_spec_file, this handles binary files and files up to 50 MiB, and the response returns only metadata (saved path, size, revision) — not the content. Use it to save a large or binary file locally, then search or read it in chunks with other tools.

revision.description: Specific revision number to download (defaults to the latest revision).

destination_path.description: Local path to save the file to. Optional: omit it to save the file under `.specs/` in the MCP server's working directory, mirroring its remote path (`specs/add-oauth/proposal.md` → `.specs/add-oauth/proposal.md`). When given, it is absolute or relative to that working directory; a relative path rooted at `specs/` is redirected to `.specs/`, so pass an absolute path to save into a literal `specs/` directory. If it points to an existing directory (or ends with a path separator), the spec file's basename is appended.

overwrite.description: Overwrite the destination file if it already exists (default: false).

tools.name: list_spec_file
tools.description: List a project's spec files with id, path, and metadata (revision count, file size of the latest revision, file type, owning session, last update). Filter to a directory with `path` (exact file or everything under it; pass "", "/", or omit for all). Set `trashed=true` to list files in the Trash Bin instead of live files. Ordered by `file_path` ascending whenever `path` or `trashed` is given, most-recently-created first otherwise. Returns `total` and, when more records remain, `next_offset`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose spec files to list.

path.description: Directory prefix to filter by, e.g. ".spec" or ".spec/design". Matches the exact file and everything under that directory. Pass "", "/", or omit to list all files.

trashed.description: When true, list files in the project Trash Bin instead. When false or omitted, list only live files (trashed files excluded).

limit.description: Max files to return (default 50, capped at 200).

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Get attachment metadata. With `include_download_url>0`, also returns a signed `download_url`.

include_download_url.description: Set to any positive value to include a signed download URL. Omit or 0 to skip.

tools.name: upload_attachment
tools.description: Upload a local file as a new attachment on a project. Reads `file_path` from the host running the MCP server, computes its SHA256, then performs the two-phase platform upload. Max 10 MB. Supported content: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP), and any UTF-8 text file (XML, JSON, YAML, HTML, SVG, Markdown, CSV, source code, ...). Other binary files are rejected by the platform.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to attach the file to.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the local file to upload. The MCP server reads this path from its own host.

file_name.description: Override the filename recorded on the attachment. Defaults to the path basename.

mime_type.description: Override the MIME type sent to the platform. The platform re-detects from content, so this is only a hint. If omitted, inferred from the file extension — structured (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx) keep their canonical MIME; common UTF-8 text formats (.xml, .json, .yaml, .html, .csv, .md, source code, ...) are sent as text/plain.

override.description: When true, any existing (non-deleted) attachment on the project whose recorded filename exactly matches `file_name` (or the path basename) is soft-deleted before the new upload, so the new attachment keeps the original name instead of getting an auto-dedup `(1)` suffix. The platform has no in-place content-replace API, so the new upload always gets a new `attachment_id`; any replaced ids are returned as `overridden_attachment_ids` (array, possibly empty) so callers can refresh stored references. Defaults to false (let the platform auto-dedup).

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project. Returns the created project id and metadata.

name.description: Name of the project to create.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Update a project's metadata (name, description, project_type). Returns the updated metadata.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to update.

project_type.description: Codebase type. 'greenfield' or 'brownfield' sets it explicitly; 'auto' clears it so the workflow decides. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: archive_project
tools.description: Archive a project (sets status to "archived"). Idempotent: archiving an already-archived project succeeds.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to archive.

tools.name: unarchive_project
tools.description: Unarchive a project (sets status to "active"). Idempotent: unarchiving an already-active project succeeds.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to unarchive.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Soft-delete a project. Only a project that is already archived can be deleted. If the project is still active, this tool refuses and you must NOT archive it on the user's behalf to make the deletion go through — instead, reconfirm with the user whether deleting the project is truly intended.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to delete.

tools.name: upload_spec_file
tools.description: Upload a new, session-less spec file into a project. Provide the file body inline via `content` or by pointing at a local file with `local_file_path` — exactly one is required. Prefer `local_file_path` when the body is already an existing local file (the server reads it directly, avoiding sending large content through the model); use `content` for text generated in-memory. Rejects if a file already exists at the same path (use update_spec_file to overwrite).

project_id.description: UUID of the project to upload the file into.

file_path.description: Path of the new spec file, rooted at "specs" or "openspec" with at most 3 directory levels below the root (e.g. specs/changes/add-oauth-login/proposal.md).

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content of the spec file. Provide this OR local_file_path (exactly one). Use for in-memory / generated content.

local_file_path.description: Path to a local file whose bytes become the spec file body; the server reads it directly. Provide this OR content (exactly one). Absolute paths are most reliable; a relative path resolves against the MCP server working directory. Point this only at an intended spec file — its bytes are uploaded to the project as-is; never use it for secrets or unrelated files.

file_type.description: Spec file type. Omit to derive from the filename (e.g. proposal.md → proposal).

tools.name: update_spec_file
tools.description: Overwrite an existing spec file by saving a new revision. Provide the new body inline via `content` or by pointing at a local file with `local_file_path` — exactly one is required. Prefer `local_file_path` when the body is already an existing local file (the server reads it directly); use `content` for text generated in-memory. Reference the file by file_id or by (project_id + file_path). Pass `expected_version` from the get_spec_file you based the new body on so a concurrent edit by someone else is reported instead of silently overwritten.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file to overwrite. Provide this or (project_id + file_path).

project_id.description: UUID of the project. Required (with file_path) when file_id is not given.

file_path.description: Path of the spec file. Required (with project_id) when file_id is not given.

content.description: Full UTF-8 replacement content, saved as a new revision. Provide this OR local_file_path (exactly one). Use for in-memory / generated content.

local_file_path.description: Path to a local file whose bytes become the new revision; the server reads it directly. Provide this OR content (exactly one). Absolute paths are most reliable; a relative path resolves against the MCP server working directory. Point this only at an intended spec file — its bytes are uploaded to the project as-is; never use it for secrets or unrelated files.

expected_version.description: The content_version the new body was based on, from the get_spec_file or read_spec_file you worked from. The update is rejected with an actionable error if someone else changed the file since. Omit only when overwriting unconditionally is genuinely intended — the project may be configured to reject unversioned updates.

tools.name: move_spec_file_to_trash
tools.description: Move a spec file to the Trash Bin. This is recoverable — the file is hidden from the default file list and AI-agent tools but kept restorable indefinitely via `restore_spec_file_from_trash`. It is NOT a permanent delete.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file to move to the Trash Bin.

tools.name: move_spec_folder
tools.description: Move or rename a folder under specs/ together with everything in it. The folder can be a bundle (it holds spec files directly) or a group folder holding bundles. The files of a bundle always move together; single files cannot be moved out of a bundle. File ids, contents and revisions stay the same; only paths change, so address the files by their new paths afterwards. Refused: OpenSpec folders, specs/memory, a target inside the folder itself, a target that already exists (Trash included) or sits inside a bundle, a folder inside a bundle (move the bundle instead), a folder whose bundle is still generating, and a move that would nest a bundle more than 3 levels below specs/.

project_id.description: UUID of the project holding the folder.

from_path.description: Folder to move, under "specs" (e.g. specs/mcp or specs/mcp/my-bundle).

to_path.description: New folder path: "specs" plus 1-3 lowercase kebab-case segments (e.g. specs/archive/mcp). Under the same parent, this renames the folder.

tools.name: restore_spec_file_from_trash
tools.description: Restore a spec file from the Trash Bin back to the active file list, reversing `move_spec_file_to_trash`. The file becomes visible again to the default file list and AI-agent tools.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file to restore from the Trash Bin.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: List a project's attachments (metadata only, always including file_size_bytes so a caller can check the size before read_attachment). Returns `total` and, when more records remain, `next_offset`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose attachments to list.

limit.description: Max attachments to return (default 50, capped at 200).

tools.name: read_attachment
tools.description: Return an attachment's content inline. UTF-8 text is paginated by line (offset/limit, 1 MiB per response). Images (png, jpeg, gif, webp) are returned whole as an MCP image block — never paginated — up to the 10 MiB attachment limit; a 10 MiB image is roughly 13.4 MiB of base64, so check file_size_bytes (from get_attachment or list_attachments) before reading a large one. Other binary types (pdf, docx, xlsx, …) cannot be read here; view them in the MySpec webapp.

attachment_id.description: UUID of the attachment to read

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from (text attachments only; default 1; 0 is an alias for 1).

limit.description: Max lines to return (text attachments only; default 2000, capped at 2000).

tools.name: list_spec_sessions
tools.description: List a project's spec sessions (metadata plus session_summary and context_size_bytes — never the context itself or the chat transcript). Filter with archive_filter ('active'/'archived'/'all'), status, and query (searches the session summary). Capped at 20 per page; returns `total` and `next_offset`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose spec sessions to list.

query.description: Search term matched against the session summary.

limit.description: Max sessions to return (default 10, capped at 20).

tools.name: get_spec_session
tools.description: Get one spec session's metadata: status, counters, timestamps, archived_at (delete eligibility), session_summary, plus context_size_bytes and context_keys describing the context without returning it. Set include_context=true for the full context (1 MiB ceiling). The chat transcript is never returned.

include_context.description: When true, include the whole context JSONB (subject to a 1 MiB ceiling — above it the tool errors with the actual size). Default false: the response instead carries context_size_bytes and context_keys so you can see the size and shape before asking.

tools.name: rename_spec_session
tools.description: Rename a spec session by updating its context.sessionSummary — the session's human-readable title (there is no first-class name field). Permitted on both active and archived sessions. All other context keys are preserved untouched.

session_id.description: UUID of the spec session to rename

session_summary.description: New human-readable session title (max 500 characters). Stored as context.sessionSummary — the field the webapp displays and searches.

tools.name: archive_spec_session
tools.description: Archive a spec session. Archiving is the confirmation step required before delete_spec_session, and is reversible via unarchive_spec_session. Idempotent: archiving an already-archived session succeeds and keeps the original archived_at.

session_id.description: UUID of the spec session to archive

tools.name: unarchive_spec_session
tools.description: Unarchive a spec session, returning it to the active list.

session_id.description: UUID of the spec session to unarchive

tools.name: delete_spec_session
tools.description: Soft-delete a spec session. Only an ARCHIVED session can be deleted — archive it first with archive_spec_session. This tool never archives on your behalf: archiving is the user's confirmation step, and collapsing the two-step destructive flow would remove the only checkpoint the platform provides. Check archived_at via get_spec_session to see whether delete is permitted.

session_id.description: UUID of the spec session to delete

tools.name: list_artifacts
tools.description: List a project's live artifacts (multi-file bundles such as HTML mockups, each versioned as one snapshot) with id, slug, entry path and revision_count. Returns `total` and, when more remain, `next_offset`. Use get_artifact for the file manifest and read_artifact_file for content.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose artifacts to list.

limit.description: Max artifacts to return (default 50, capped at 100).

tools.name: get_artifact
tools.description: Get an artifact's metadata plus the file manifest (path, content type, size, checksum of every file) of its head revision, or of `revision` when given. `revision_count` is the head number AND the value to pass as expected_version when writing; it only ever grows because rollback appends a revision rather than discarding history.

revision.description: Revision whose manifest to return (defaults to the head revision).

tools.name: read_artifact_file
tools.description: Return one artifact file's UTF-8 content, paginated by line (offset/limit, default and cap 2000 lines, 1 MiB per response) with `total_lines`, `truncated` and `next_offset`. Reads the head revision unless `revision` is given. Binary files (images, fonts) cannot be read through this tool; get_artifact lists their size and checksum.

path.description: Bundle-relative path of the file (e.g. index.html, assets/app.js).

revision.description: Revision to read from (defaults to the head revision).

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from (default 1; 0 is an alias for 1).

limit.description: Max lines to return (default 2000, capped at 2000; larger values are clamped).

tools.name: create_artifact
tools.description: Create an artifact — a bundle of files (e.g. an HTML mockup: index.html + styles.css + app.js) the platform versions AS ONE snapshot — with the given files as revision 1. At most 50 files, 2 MiB per file, 10 MiB per revision. Fails with a conflict when the slug is already taken in the project (trashed artifacts still own their slug).

project_id.description: UUID of the project to create the artifact in.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier, unique within the project; derived from the name when omitted.

entry_path.description: The file a renderer opens first. Defaults to index.html when present, else the only file.

message.description: Short summary of this first revision (max 500 characters).

path.description: Bundle-relative path, "/"-separated, no leading slash (e.g. assets/logo.svg).

encoding.description: utf8 (default) for text; base64 for binary files such as images.

content_type.description: Hint used only for extensions the platform does not recognise.

tools.name: write_artifact_revision
tools.description: Write a new revision of an artifact. FULL mode (no base_revision): `files` becomes the whole bundle. PATCH mode (base_revision set): only the changed files are sent, plus `remove` for paths to drop — the platform stores the complete result either way. Every revision is immutable; the newest N are retained (50 by default, set by the platform; older ones are pruned); use rollback_artifact to restore an earlier one. Read the current head with get_artifact first and pass its revision_count as expected_version.

path.description: Bundle-relative path, "/"-separated, no leading slash (e.g. assets/logo.svg).

encoding.description: utf8 (default) for text; base64 for binary files such as images.

content_type.description: Hint used only for extensions the platform does not recognise.

base_revision.description: PATCH mode: start from this revision's files, upsert `files` by path and drop `remove` paths. Omit for FULL mode, where `files` is the complete new file set. Patch mode defaults expected_version to base_revision.

remove.description: Patch mode only: paths to drop from the base revision.

expected_version.description: The revision_count this write is based on (from get_artifact). The platform refuses the write with a conflict if the head moved. Defaults to base_revision in patch mode, else the current head.

message.description: Short summary of the change (max 500 characters).

entry_path.description: Change the file a renderer opens first, from this revision on.

tools.name: rollback_artifact
tools.description: Restore an earlier revision of an artifact. Like `git revert`, this APPENDS a new revision whose files equal the chosen one — history is never rewritten, and the new head is revision_count + 1. Only the newest N revisions are retained (50 by default, set by the platform): older ones are pruned, and rolling back to a pruned revision fails with not found — list the revisions (get_artifact) first when in doubt. Rolling back to the head itself is allowed and recorded with no_change=true.

revision_number.description: The revision whose files to restore.

expected_version.description: The revision_count this rollback is based on (from get_artifact); defaults to the current head.

message.description: Optional summary; defaults to "Rolled back to revision N".

tools.name: create_stream_token
tools.description: Create a short-lived WebSocket URL that streams a project's events in real time — like an S3 presigned URL, the returned URL is the whole credential and needs no auth header. Choose the project and the event types to follow; the result carries the full wss:// URL. Feed it to any WebSocket client with subprotocol 'v1' (for example Claude Code's Monitor tool). Each text frame is one JSON event carrying a `seq` cursor; reconnect with ?after=<seq> to resume without missing events. Defaults to 24 hours, 7 days maximum. TREAT THE RETURNED URL LIKE A PASSWORD: anyone holding it can read every event on this project until it expires, without authenticating. Pass it directly to the WebSocket client; never write it to a file, a commit, an issue or a chat reply, and never log or repeat it. It is shown once and cannot be retrieved again. If it may have been exposed, revoke it at once with revoke_stream_token — that is also how you end one early. Prefer the shortest ttl_seconds that covers the work.

resource_type.description: What to follow. Only 'project' is supported today.

resource_id.description: UUID of the project to stream events for.

event_types.description: Event types to receive. Required — pass ["*"] to follow all of them. spec_file.updated covers new revisions, rollbacks, and moves to or from the trash; spec_file.lock covers acquire, renew, release and takeover; spec_session.updated covers completion, archive, unarchive and rename; spec_file_comment.updated covers a body edit and a soft delete, thread_state_changed covers resolve and unresolve, and anchors_updated is batched across every thread one save moved.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the URL stays valid. Defaults to 24 hours, capped at 7 days. Out-of-range values are clamped rather than rejected — check expires_at in the result.

label.description: Short human-readable label, so a person can recognise this token in a listing.

tools.name: list_stream_tokens
tools.description: List the stream tokens in your organisation, with their scope, expiry and whether each is still live. Secrets are never returned — only a short prefix to tell tokens apart. Returns `total` and, when more remain, `next_offset`.

mine_only.description: Only tokens you created. Off by default, so a leaked URL can be found — note that revoking one you did not mint needs the organisation owner or admin role.

limit.description: Max tokens to return (default 50, capped at 200).

tools.name: revoke_stream_token
tools.description: Revoke a stream token immediately, closing its URL and deleting the events buffered for it. Use this as soon as a stream is no longer needed, or if its URL may have leaked — the URL is the credential, so revoking is the only way to stop it before it expires. Revoking a token you minted yourself always works. Revoking one somebody ELSE minted additionally requires the organisation owner or admin role, and is refused with 403 otherwise — so when hunting a leaked URL you did not create, expect that refusal and ask an organisation owner or admin rather than retrying.

id.description: Token id (from create_stream_token or list_stream_tokens) — NOT the secret itself.

tools.name: start_spec_session
tools.description: Start a NEW MySpec chat session on the user's behalf with an opening prompt you compose, run its first turn, and hand back a URL for the user to continue in the MySpec webapp. Compose the prompt yourself from what you know about this repository and the user's intent — that context is the whole point, and it is lost if the user has to retype it. ONE invocation starts exactly ONE real chat session and consumes model tokens billed to the token owner, so call it ONCE PER INTENT, never in a loop. After a timeout or a transport error, call list_spec_sessions BEFORE invoking again — the session may already exist, and a retry would create a duplicate. Your responsibility ENDS at relaying the returned session_url to the user: do NOT attempt to drive the MySpec workflow yourself. Arguments: project_id, mode (generate | edit) and prompt are required; workflow_id, language, model_id, attachment_ids, spec_file_ids and session_title are optional. Returns session_url, assistant_text, session_id, project_id, pending_action and next_step_instruction; plus first_turn_error when the session was created but its first turn could not run, and (stdio only) warnings when something about the setup will limit the session — neither of which means the session is missing, so relay session_url either way. BROWNFIELD WORKFLOWS: start the reverse-MCP bridge with `npx -y @myspec/mcp-server reverse --root <path>` BEFORE calling this tool, so the very first turn can already read the local codebase. Keep the bridge RUNNING after this tool returns — the session keeps reading the local codebase while the user works in the webapp.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to start the session in.

mode.description: 'generate' writes a new spec bundle from scratch; 'edit' changes the spec files of an existing bundle.

prompt.description: The opening message. Write it as the user would: what they want specced, and the repository context you have gathered that they would otherwise have to retype.

workflow_id.description: Workflow variant id, e.g. myspec-greenfield-v1, enterprise-greenfield-v1, speckit-greenfield-v1, openspec-brownfield-v1, myspec-brownfield-v1, myspec-edit-v1, myspec-edit-brownfield-v1. Omit to use the default for the chosen mode. Must agree with mode — a contradiction is rejected, not silently resolved.

language.description: Output language the session locks to on its first turn. Defaults to 'en'. A session's language is immutable once set.

model_id.description: Model id to run the session with, e.g. openai:gpt-6-sol.

attachment_ids.description: Project attachment ids to cite in the opening message, as the composer @-mentions do. At most 25.

spec_file_ids.description: Existing spec file ids to cite in the opening message. Required in practice for edit sessions. At most 25.

session_title.description: Human-readable session title, stored as context.sessionSummary (max 500 characters). A workflow that names the session itself during its interview will overwrite it, exactly as in the webapp.

tools.name: list_spec_file_comments
tools.description: List the review comment threads on a spec file. Each thread carries the passage it is anchored to, whether it is resolved, its anchor status, and its comments. Works on a trashed file as well as a live one. Read this before editing a file under review. Returns at most 100 threads (with total_threads and truncated) and previews each comment body to 1000 characters, flagging it with body_truncated; narrow with `status` to see fewer threads in full.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file whose comments to list.

status.description: Narrow to open (unresolved) threads, resolved ones, or orphaned ones whose passage can no longer be located. Omit for all of them.

tools.name: create_spec_file_comment_thread
tools.description: Open a review comment on a specific passage of a spec file. Quote the passage exactly as it appears. Do NOT send character offsets — the server locates the quote itself. Refused with a conflict on a trashed file: a file staged for deletion does not gather new discussion.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file to comment on.

anchor_quote.description: The exact passage this comment is about, copied verbatim from the file. The server searches the current content for it, so it must match the text as written. Read the file with read_spec_file first. At most 2000 characters.

anchor_prefix.description: The text immediately BEFORE the quote, which disambiguates a passage appearing more than once. At most 64 characters — a few words, not a sentence. Send an empty string when the quote starts the file.

anchor_suffix.description: The text immediately AFTER the quote. At most 64 characters. Empty when the quote ends the file.

tools.name: reply_spec_file_comment_thread
tools.description: Reply to an existing review comment thread on a spec file. Use this to answer a reviewer's question or report what you changed. Refused with a conflict on a trashed file.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file the thread belongs to.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to reply to, from list_spec_file_comments.

tools.name: update_spec_file_comment
tools.description: Edit the body of one of YOUR OWN comments on a spec file. The platform refuses a comment written by somebody else. Pass the comment's own content_version as expected_version to avoid overwriting an edit made since you read it. Works on a trashed file.

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file the comment belongs to.

comment_id.description: UUID of the comment to edit. Must be your own.

body.description: The replacement text, in markdown. Replaces the comment entirely.

expected_version.description: The COMMENT's own content_version as last read by list_spec_file_comments — not the file's. Sending it makes the edit fail rather than silently overwrite one made since.

tools.name: delete_spec_file_comment
tools.description: Soft-delete one of YOUR OWN comments on a spec file. Three outcomes, reported in the result: a reply simply disappears (comment: null); a first comment with live replies becomes a tombstone so the thread keeps a head (comment: the tombstone); and a first comment with no live replies takes the whole thread (thread_deleted: true).

file_id.description: UUID of the spec file the comment belongs to.

comment_id.description: UUID of the comment to delete. Must be your own.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List a project's tasks: every checkbox task in its tasks.md files, in file order, each with a stable task_id, status (pending, in_progress, done), assignee, priority (0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low), story points, cycle, start/end dates (YYYY-MM-DD), labels and relationships with other tasks ({type, task_id}: this task blocks, is blocked_by, or is related to that task). Also returns the files (with the content_version their tasks reflect), and the labels and cycles in use. Filter by status, assignee ("me" for yourself, "none" for unassigned), cycle, label or file. Paged: 100 tasks by default (limit up to 500), with total_tasks and, while more remain, next_offset. Details (sub-bullets) only with include_details. Use the task_id values with update_tasks and set_task_status.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose tasks to list.

assignee_user_id.description: Only tasks assigned to this user id (as returned in assignee_user_id or by list_task_assignees). "me" means you; "none" means unassigned tasks.

cycle.description: Only tasks in this cycle (sprint) number.

file_id.description: Only tasks from this tasks.md (its spec file id).

include_details.description: Also return each task's details (its sub-bullets in tasks.md), previewed to 500 characters. Off by default: they make the result several times larger.

offset.description: How many matching tasks to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: list_task_assignees
tools.description: List who a project's tasks can be assigned to: the organisation's people who can open the project, which is exactly who update_tasks accepts as assignee_user_id. Each has a user_id, a username (handle) and a display_name ("" when unset). Also returns your own user id as self_user_id. May include people who have left the organisation but whose profile remains. At most 1000 people; truncated is true when the list was cut.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose tasks are being assigned.

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Edit the planning fields of one or more tasks: assignee, priority, story points, cycle, start and due dates, labels, and relationships with other tasks (blocks, blocked_by, related). The same change applies to every task given. A field left out is left alone; null clears it. Labels and relationships are added and removed, not replaced. Does not change status or the task's text, which live in tasks.md: use set_task_status for status. All or nothing: an unknown task id fails the whole call. Returns the tasks as they are now.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the tasks belong to.

task_ids.description: The tasks to change (task_id values from list_tasks). At most 200 per call.

assignee_user_id.description: User id to assign ("me" for yourself), or null to unassign. The person must be a member of the organisation who can open the project: list_task_assignees lists them.

story_points.description: Estimate in story points, or null to clear it.

cycle.description: Cycle (sprint) number, or null to clear it.

start_date.description: Start day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear it.

end_date.description: Due day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear it. Not before the start day.

add_labels.description: Labels to add. A task carries at most 20.

add_relationships.description: Relationships to set. Two tasks have at most one: setting one replaces whatever the pair had, and the other task sees the inverse (A blocks B is B blocked_by A). A task has at most 50.

type.description: How each changed task stands to task_id: blocks (task_id waits for it), blocked_by (it waits for task_id) or related.

task_id.description: The other task (a task_id from list_tasks).

remove_relationships.description: Task ids to unlink each changed task from, whatever the relationship.

tools.name: set_task_status
tools.description: Change the status of one or more tasks by rewriting their checkbox in the project's tasks.md files: `[ ]` pending, `[-]` in progress, `[x]` done. Each affected file gets one new revision, recorded as an AI change; nothing else in the file changes. Partial by nature: a file that cannot be written (it kept changing, it changed since the expected_versions you passed, the organisation is out of storage, or it was moved to the trash) fails only its own tasks. Returns an outcome per task (updated, unchanged, removed: no longer in its file, failed: with an error code), an outcome per file, and the tasks as they are now. Marked as an error only when every task failed.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the tasks belong to.

task_ids.description: The tasks to move (task_id values from list_tasks). At most 200 per call.

status.description: The new status: pending, in_progress or done.

expected_versions.description: Optional. The file versions your view of these tasks came from (from list_tasks); only the files these tasks are in are checked, so passing just those is enough. A file that has changed since is not written and its tasks fail with file_changed, so a change never lands on a line you did not see; list again and retry.

content_version.description: The content_version list_tasks returned for that file.
